clue.text: Cyclone had rolled stone

indicators.note: something rolled is tumbled over and over, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tornado sent a big rock tumbling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' rearranges CYCLONEHAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalcedony is a kind of quartz, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Rocky knocked out leader in town

indicators.note: the leader of the word is knocked out, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A boxer called Rocky was floored by the champion in town.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNSTABLE is an English town in Bedfordshire; 'knocked out leader' drops its first letter D. 'Rocky' looks like the boxer but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocky is shaky and wobbly, not steady.

clue.text: Cut off, wanting 5 to grow furious

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following item is taken away

parts.note: cut off means severed
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone cut off without five pounds is getting angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is simply the number, V in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming very angry.

clue.text: Burn fish after removing its head

indicators.note: the head of the fish word, its first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a brill is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Cooking a fish once its head has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is not to scorch here: it is the Scottish word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Burn is a Scottish word for a stream, and a rill is a small brook.

clue.text: Small mammal turning on the vicar

indicators.note: turning means twisting round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little animal suddenly attacks the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges ONTHEVICAR. A chevrotain is a tiny deer-like animal, the mouse deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The chevrotain, or mouse deer, is a tiny hoofed mammal.

clue.text: Spanish artist depicting little woman remade Marion

parts.note: Jo is one of the sisters in Little Women

indicators.note: remade means made again in a new form, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter shows a small lady who has been given a makeover named Marion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remade' turns MARION into ANMIRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a Catalan surrealist painter from Barcelona.

clue.text: Musical feature of Surrey — band appearing in Farnham and Ewell initially

indicators.note: appearing in puts the band inside the other letters
initially takes the first letters of the two town names

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A Surrey arts festival features a band playing in two of the county's towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey reads as the English county, home of Farnham and Ewell, but it is the carriage in the Oklahoma! song The Surrey with the Fringe on Top.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's horse-drawn surrey has a decorative trim of hanging threads on its top.

clue.text: Burn fish

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken by fire
a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes

explanation.definitionFit: Char means to scorch, and the char is a fish related to trout.

clue.text: Composer gets back to record company with the "Unfinished"

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
EMI is a British record company

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A composer is tied to his label alongside a famous Unfinished symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The "Unfinished" suggests Schubert's symphony, but it only cuts the last letter from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Hindemith was a twentieth-century German composer.

clue.text: Brother who didn't speak about TV star

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Harpo was the silent Marx Brother

explanation.surface: A silent monk is talking about a television celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' suggests a monk under a vow of silence; it is the mute Marx Brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey is a famous American television host.

clue.text: Succeeding almost totally on the side

parts.note: succeeding means coming afterwards, later

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, dropping its last letter

parts.note: totally means all, in full

explanation.surface: Someone is doing well almost entirely through a sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, sideways.

clue.text: Opening number — singer's last resort

parts.note: a vent is an opening

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the singer's word

explanation.surface: An opening song is a vocalist's final fallback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' reads as a phrase, but 'last' belongs to the singer and 'resort' is the definition. Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventnor is a seaside holiday town on the Isle of Wight off England's south coast.

clue.text: Award accepted by Erasmus Darwin, primarily for plant

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the award goes within the other letters
primarily takes the first letter of each name

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Erasmus Darwin, Charles's grandfather and a botanist, receives an honour for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a botanical noun, fitting Erasmus Darwin, but it is the verb to fix firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to set it firmly in place, to fix it deep within.

clue.text: Primary school table about right for deceiving people?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the table goes round the letter

parts.note: the two times table is learnt in primary school

explanation.surface: A multiplication table learnt in junior school is wrapped round a word for correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timers are cheats who are unfaithful to their partners.

clue.text: Follower of 11 who has one-off chance to play?

definitions.text: Follower of 11 who has one-off chance to play?

parts.words: Follower of 11 who has one-off chance to play?
parts.note: a cricket team has eleven players, and the reserve who comes next in line may get a single chance to take the field

explanation.walkthrough: 11 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is the number of players in a cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the reserve after the eleven players substitutes in the field only when needed.

clue.text: Dance with shyster apt to twist

indicators.note: to twist means to bend out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer is ready to do a twisting dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to twist' rearranges SHYSTERAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish dance, named after the valley of the Spey.

clue.text: 11 in succession

definitions.meaning: the figure is literally a one followed by a one

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consecutively, and the figure written as two ones shows one placed after one.

clue.text: Prosper like Dusty Miller?

parts.note: a miller is dusty with flour
-ish is a suffix meaning like or somewhat

explanation.surface: A singer called Dusty Miller is thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Dusty Miller reads as a name, but a miller is dusty from flour.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive or do well.

clue.text: Ignoring cold sausage, Poles find meeting places, apparently

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: chorizo is a spicy Spanish sausage
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people skip the cold sausage and find somewhere to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but gives the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyline is where earth and sky seem to meet, hence 'apparently'.

clue.text: Shout now, if that is flaky tuna

parts.note: to yell is to shout

indicators.note: flaky means falling apart into flakes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cries out that the tuna has gone flaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaky' rearranges NOWIF into OWFIN; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowfin is a species of tuna found in warm seas.

clue.text: Songs the kaiser heard?

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, so one that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: the German kaiser was his nation's leader

explanation.surface: Asks whether the German emperor ever heard any songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder are German art songs, fitting the kaiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Following Irish saint at the outset

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Coming after an Irish saint right from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: First means at the beginning, initially.

clue.text: Light and delicate feature of a parade on the Fourth of July

parts.note: a float is a decorated vehicle in a parade

indicators.note: fourth of takes the fourth letter of the word

explanation.surface: Gauzy decorations for a parade vehicle on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fourth of July looks like American Independence Day, but it gives the fourth letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: A floaty fabric is light and airy, seeming to float.

clue.text: A hunter goes to pot? Grub up!

indicators.note: goes to pot means falls into ruin, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hunter's game ends up in the pot: dinner is served!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub up!' looks like a call to dinner, but it means dig up.
explanation.definitionFit: To grub up is to dig out of the ground.

clue.text: Language used by Monsieur Dumas

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by the French writer Dumas.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

clue.text: British and French, 11 small works of art

parts.note: onze is French for eleven

explanation.surface: British and French sculptures shown in a small group of eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like a nationality beside British, but it says the number is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronzes are sculptures cast in bronze.

clue.text: Weep when coming up with potential bloomer

indicators.note: coming up means rising in a down entry, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to blub is to cry

explanation.surface: Someone cries when their future flower comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder to cry over; it is something that will bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb is a plant that may in time produce a flower.

clue.text: Garb for bride or groom

definitions.meaning: to groom is to arrange or tidy, as hair or a horse

explanation.definitionFit: A bride wears a gown, and to groom is to dress hair or a horse.

clue.text: Suddenly Arthur's beginning to suspect Lancelot

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of the king's name
suspect as an adjective means doubtful, so the name's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: King Arthur abruptly starts to distrust Lancelot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suspect' rearranges LANCELOT into LLATONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means abruptly, without warning.
